overall_summary: FACTVERSE's audience shows a massive preference for extreme space anomalies, exoplanets, and immersive 'What-If' cosmic survival scenarios. Traditional psychology and repetitive animal trivia consistently underperform, whereas high-concept cosmic threats and bizarre planetary environments drive the highest views and engagement.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' achieved 970 views, 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' reached 1,025 views, and 'What If You Fell Into This $26 Nonillion Diamond Planet?' secured 494 views with high like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Pivot content strategy heavily toward cosmic survival scenarios, focusing on first-person 'What If' journeys into the universe's most hostile environments.

winning_patterns.pattern: High-Contrast Visual & Sensory Hooks in Titles
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring extreme sensory juxtapositions like 'Burning Ice' (1,055 views) and 'Supersonic Rubies' (721 views) significantly outperform generic titles.
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate vivid, tactile, and high-contrast imagery in the first 3 seconds of both the title and the visual hook (e.g., liquid metal, glass winds, dark coal).

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' repeatedly failed to gain traction across multiple uploads, peaking at only 53 views. 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' stalled at 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Phase out soft science and generic brain hacks unless they can be framed through a high-stakes, cinematic mystery lens.

weak_patterns.pattern: Basic Animal Facts Without Narrative Stakes
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' and 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' struggled to break past low-baseline views, showing weak organic push.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid dry encyclopedic animal facts. If covering wildlife, pivot to the 'cinematic animal survival' niche with high-drama storytelling.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Planet of Molten Iron Rain?
next_video.opening_direction: Show a cinematic first-person POV of a spacesuit melting in mid-air with the voiceover: 'If you fell into WASP-76b, your death wouldn't just be instant—it would be metallic.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet's night side is cold enough to turn iron vapor into liquid metal rain, meaning you would literally be pelted to death by molten iron droplets.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful 'What If' format combined with extreme planetary weather, matching the 21-second duration of top-performing cosmic Shorts.

experiment: Test a 3-part micro-series focusing on 'Cosmic Horrors We Can See From Earth', starting with the closest black hole, utilizing high-contrast cinematic visuals and a deep, ominous voiceover tone.
